name: Battle radio man, USA, Normandy 1944 (our own design)
about: Made by Tools/battle_units/soldier_usa_radio.py on soldier_usa.py and soldier.py. Metres; x forward, y right, z up. Paints: 0 tunic, 1 trousers, 2 boots, 3 lower, 4 straps, 5 helmet, 6 pack, 7 skin, 8 wood, 9 steel, 10 coat, 11 coat_dark, 12 leather, 13 blanket, 14 hoof, 19 radio (the eyes are painted as boots). near = LOD0, mid = LOD1, far = LOD2, all in the rest pose (arms 45 degrees down). Each point rides on bone `part` and, by `w2` (0 to 0.5), on bone `part2`. Skinning: a bone's turn G = G_parent * q (q from the clip, identity at rest; G of a bone with no track is its parent's), its head X = X_parent + G_parent * (head - head_parent + move), and a point p on it goes to X + G * (p - head). Quaternions are [t, w, x, y, z] in these axes (as Unreal's FQuat). Clips are in place: `stride` is the metres one loop covers; the game moves the unit. A mesh may carry `shade` per point (0 to 1, the wear and seam darkening): its colour is the paint's colour times shade; with no `shade` every point is 1. He is the company's radio man: soldier_usa.py's rifleman (dress, helmet, canteen, first-aid pouch) with the M1 carbine on the weapon bone (0.904 m; semi-automatic: his fire_stand, fire_kneel and fire_prone are soldier_usa.py's, one shot a second, cue rifle_shot), a pistol belt with a pocket of two carbine magazines, and on his back in the haversack's place the SCR-300 set over its battery case (paint 19, radio) with its long whip antenna (3.25 m, up from the set's top left, leaning a little back and out to his left; on its own four bones, below). The handset rides the bolt bone: clipped high on his left suspender strap in every clip, in his left hand and at his left ear in radio_call. His own: radio_call (8 s loop, kneeling, his carbine laid by his left knee): the handset taken off the strap (0.85 s) and put to his ear, radio_squelch at 1.5 s (cue radio_squelch, on the head); he calls, radio_talk at 1.95 s (cue radio_talk, on the head), turns his head to the target and points to it with his right hand; call_support at 5.3 s (no socket, no cue): the call goes through and the battle decides what comes, artillery or an airstrike; he hears the answer and nods, and hangs the handset back on the strap (7.25 s). For an airstrike (in 1944 the target was marked with coloured smoke) the game can mark it with his throw_grenade clip (its grenade_release event) as a coloured smoke grenade. lmg_burst (prone on the aim) fires nothing. The whip is a chain of four bones for the deaths to bend: whip_1 (a child of chest, its head at the antenna's mount on top of the set) to whip_4, laid end to end up the whip to its tip (whip_1 0.86 m, through the base to the second ferrule; the others 0.8125 m each), after the 32 bones (bones 32 to 35, here and in the glb's skin). Near, each section of the whip rides its bone and the ferrules at the joints take the two bones half and half; mid and far, the whip is one straight tube from its foot (whip_1) to its tip (whip_4). In every clip the chain is straight, at rest, but for a gentle sway in walk, run and advance (a few degrees at each joint).

stretcher_front.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, the arms keyed to the poles
stretcher_front.about: The front man of a two-man stretcher (the Stretcher prop, battle-models/ground-props), walking at about 0.75 m/s (stride 1.058 m a 1.42 s cycle), head down, the prop's grip.front.left/right in his fists: `grips` (his left fist then his right, every key, the root's frame, the game's axes; `mean` their average). Play stretcher_front and stretcher_rear on one clock (same phase, in step). Place the prop's root at the mean of the four fists less 0.14 m, head end (+x) toward the front man; then his root x = the prop's x + 1.1 - his grips' mean x. The carried man (carried_wounded) at the prop's `lie`. The rifle rides slung on his back.

stretcher_rear.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, the arms keyed to the poles
stretcher_rear.about: The rear man of a two-man stretcher (the Stretcher prop, battle-models/ground-props), walking at about 0.75 m/s (stride 1.058 m a 1.42 s cycle), head down, the prop's grip.back.left/right in his fists: `grips` (his left fist then his right, every key, the root's frame, the game's axes; `mean` their average). Play stretcher_front and stretcher_rear on one clock (same phase, in step). Place the prop's root at the mean of the four fists less 0.14 m, head end (+x) toward the front man; then his root x = the prop's x - 1.1 - his grips' mean x. The carried man (carried_wounded) at the prop's `lie`. The rifle rides slung on his back.

splice_kneel.from: field_clips.py: kneel_down's last pose, the arms keyed
splice_kneel.about: The lineman at a cut wire, kneeling (kneel_down, then this, then stand_up), twisting the two ends together in his hands three times and giving it a tug (event wire_tug) to test it. The wire's two ends run into his fists at `hands` (left then right, the root's frame, the game's axes): draw each end from there down to the ground and away along the line. His reel sits on the ground by his right knee. The rifle rides slung on his back.

carried_wounded.about: The man on the stretcher, alive (the dead stay still; he does not): on his back, head to +x (the Stretcher prop's head end, carried first), breathing, his left knee drawn up and let down, his right hand on his chest, his head turning now and then. His root goes at the prop's `lie` socket, turned with it. No weapon (the weapon bone rides 2 m under his root). His white field dressing is the game's to place.

reel_walk.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, bent, the arms keyed to the reel
reel_walk.about: The lineman walking his line out, about 0.75 m/s (stride 1.058 m a 1.42 s cycle), bent forward, the CableReel prop (battle-models/ground-props) carried before him by its two handles: `reel` gives, every key, the prop's root (x, y, z) and his left and right fists (on its grip.left and grip.right), the root's frame, the game's axes; the prop faces as he does. Turn its drum by the wire paid out (the prop's README). The rifle rides slung on his back.

wounded_waiting.about: A wounded man on the ground waiting for the bearers, alive: on his back (head to +x, his root on the ground under his middle), breathing hard, his right hand pressed to the wound at his right side, his left knee drawn up and let down, his head turning, and once a loop his left arm lifted to call them. His rifle lies by his right side. When the bearers reach him: carried_wounded on the stretcher (the same lie, so it swaps without a jump but for the hands).

helmets.name: plain olive drab
helmets.about: Issue M1 in rough olive drab (cork or sawdust in the paint to kill the shine), the rim and chin-strap loops rubbed toward the steel. No badge as issued.

helmets.name: net
helmets.about: A helmet net over the plain helmet (American fine-mesh nets, or the wider British-made ones issued in England before the landings), worn bare.

helmets.name: net and burlap scrim
helmets.about: The 1944 Normandy look: the wide British-made net with strips of burlap and hessian, green and brown, pushed through it and hanging past the rim.

helmets.name: net and hedgerow leaves
helmets.about: Net with sprigs from the hedgerows of the bocage stuck through it (Normandy, June to August 1944).

helmets.name: net and jungle leaves
helmets.about: Net with broad leaves through it, in the Pacific and Burma.

helmets.name: sergeant's bar
helmets.about: A white bar painted across the back, the mark of a sergeant (officers wore it upright), as many units painted them in Europe from 1944.

helmets.name: road dust
helmets.about: The plain helmet under the white dust of the Normandy lanes in the summer breakout.

helmets.name: mud
helmets.about: Mud smeared on by hand (the autumn and winter of 1944 in Lorraine and the Hurtgen).

helmets.name: whitewash
helmets.about: Whitewash or white paint brushed over in the Ardennes snow (December 1944 to February 1945), rubbed back to the drab at the rim.

helmets.name: white cloth
helmets.about: A piece of bedsheet or mattress cover tied over the helmet in the Ardennes.

about_variety: Variety (Tools/battle_units/variety.py and helmet_finishes.py): one man made into many. `faces` (8): face 0 is the man as he is; for face k, add `move` (metres, this file's axes) to the points listed in `at`, at each level of detail, then colour: every skin-painted point's colour times `tone`, and each point in `tint_at` times its `tint` (the hair, brows, stubble or moustache), all on top of the paint (and `shade`) as usual. `helmets`: his helmet (or cap, ushanka or hood) in the finishes it was worn in. Each is a rigid mesh at near/mid/far in the same form as the file's own meshes (points, facings, paints, triangles, part, part2, w2, and shade where the file has it), with `ink` at each point: -1 paints the point by its paint number as ever; any other value is an index into `inks` (colours, RRGGBB), the colour to paint it instead. To draw a man in a finish, leave out his own helmet's triangles, `helmet_tris[lod]` = [first, count] (they are the last of the list), and draw the finish's mesh skinned on the same bones. Each finish has `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM), `season` (any, summer, winter), `front` (any, east, west, south, desert, pacific, china) and `share` (how common it was). Picking, for each man: the finishes whose months hold the battle's date and whose season and front fit (any fits all), one chosen by share, and face = a hash of (block id, k) mod 8 and the helmet from another hash of the same, so a man keeps both all battle. When no finish fits the date, draw the first finish (or his own helmet). No swastika, rising-sun flag or fascist badge is drawn: the German eagle decal is left off (its side stays plain paint).
about_deaths: Deaths (Tools/battle_units/falls.py on ragdoll.py): every die_* clip named in `deaths` is a physics fall baked from this man's own body (his parts' masses, his joints' human ranges, the muscle tone going out of him, the ground under him; the rifle leaves his hand and lands where it lands), so no two kinds fall alike and none sinks into the ground. Pick: deaths[stance][kind], stance stand, run, kneel, prone or cover (what he was doing when hit), kind as the Fates picker's man_fall kinds (forward, back, side, knees, spin, thrown) or crawl (wounded: he falls, drags himself on a little, then goes still), or where he was hit when the scene knows it: head (he drops where he stands), gut (he folds at the waist, then goes down), leg (that leg goes from under him); one of the list by a hash of (block id, man). Play it once (loop false) and hold its last frame for the rest of the battle: the body stays where it fell. Each clip starts in the pose of `start` [clip, time] (blend into it over ~0.15 s from whatever he was doing); `end_offset` is where his pelvis ends (metres, his own axes; the clip is not in place: the pelvis and the rifle move); the weapon bone's last key is the rifle lying on the ground. Events: knee_down, body_fall, rifle_drop (and elbow_down in a crawl), at the time they touch. The older die_back, die_forward and die_kneel stay in the file as they were but are not in the table (they sink into the ground). What he drops is his carbine. The handset on the bolt bone stays clipped on his left strap through every death. The SCR-300 set on his back (with its battery, about 15 kg) is part of his body: he lands on it and it weighs his chest. Its whip antenna is kept out of his shape, so it does not prop him up. The whip's own bones (whip_1 to whip_4) are keyed in each death: it sags a little where it lies level and bends over to lie along the ground where it would go under.
about_wear: Wear and weather (Tools/battle_units/shade.py; Brian, 22 November 2026: uniforms dirtier the longer a unit is at the front, fresh replacements clean; rain darkens the cloth and splashes the mud higher; snow white on the shoulders and helmets). Per point, at near, mid and far and on each helmet finish's own mesh: `shade` (0.4 to 1) and `tint` (3 a point: red, green, blue) are the look as baked, a man some weeks in the line (wear W 0.6) in dry weather, for drawing paint x shade x tint as ever. `shade_clean`: the same shadow with no dirt (folds, under the straps, pack, belt and helmet brim, worn edges, the cloth's uneven fade). `dirt` (0 to 1): where dust and mud collect in dry weather (boots, leggings and trousers to a little over the knee in splashes, the knees, the seat, elbows, cuffs and hands, a little in the face's creases); `dirt_wet`: the same in rain (mud splashed up the thighs, caked boots, heavier knees and seat, the forearms and the front of the belly from going down in it). `wet` (0 to 1): how much the surface darkens when soaked (wool 1, webbing 0.8, leather 0.6, wood 0.45, helmet paint 0.3, steel 0.2, skin 0.15; less under the pack and the arms). `snow` (0 to 1): how much snow settles there on a man standing (open to the sky and facing up: the helmet's crown, shoulders, pack, the tops of the arms and boots; little on skin and steel). MIXING, per man: W = wear, from how long his unit has been at the front (0.1 a fresh replacement or a new unit, 1 six weeks or more in the line; replacements in a veteran unit stay low until they have been in it a while), R = rain (0 dry ground to 1 soaked) and S = snow (0 to 1), both from the battle's weather draw. In sRGB 0 to 1: base = paint x shade_clean x (1 - 0.35 x wet x R) (x the face's tone and tint); d = (dirt + (dirt_wet - dirt) x R) x W; soil = (DUST + (MUD - DUST) x R) x shade_clean, DUST (0.60, 0.54, 0.43) dry dust and dried mud, MUD (0.27, 0.21, 0.15) wet mud (or the field's own soil, lighter dry); colour = base + (soil - base) x 0.85 x d; then toward snow (0.92, 0.94, 0.97) x (0.6 + 0.4 x shade_clean) by 0.9 x snow x S. The gore paints (wound, bone, blood): shade 1, no dirt, wet or snow. Mid and far carry the near's, their shade eased off (90 % and 75 % of the darkening).

face_mesh.about: Close-range face (Tools/battle_units/face_mesh.py): the near mesh's face is split finer, red-green (no crack), and its new points set on MakeHuman's man the file was cut from (seed and nation below), so lids, lips, nostrils and the folds by the nose come back; the eyeballs' fronts are split once on their own spheres. No index moves: a split triangle keeps its place with its first piece; the other pieces and the new points are on the end of near's lists (from the first new point and triangle below), so helmet_tris and the gore ranges stay true. Each new point takes its parents' bone weights, shade, wear and tint, and in each face their move, facing and tint. Mid and far are as they were.

about_run_styles: run_styles.py (release 2, 23 November 2026): run_b, run_c, run_d and advance_b, advance_c, advance_d, each another runner's motion capture (CMU 09_02, 16_36, 09_03) with this file's own hold on his weapon; style_of names the clip each is a style of; the feet planted on this file's legs, the stride fitted to them (a planted foot slides no more than in his own run). The game gives each man one of the four (LandMen, the run-styles switch); far men banked in poses play the base clip's.

ride_clips.trucks: The benches in the back of the Truck, the Hanomag and the M3 (rider.1-10: rider.1-5 on her left bench facing her right, rider.6-10 on the right): bench_ride is each seat's loop (4 s), his rifle stood between his knees in both hands; die_bench_slump its death (2.4 s, held from 1.5: he folds forward over his knees inside his own place). bench_rise_* gets him up turning toward the way out, ending upright in the aisle facing aft, his rifle at the port; bench_sit_* is the way back down, from standing in the aisle facing forward. aisle.<vehicle>.seats names each seat's rise and sit (the M3's front pair and both half-tracks' rear pair have their own: the M3's machine gun over the aisle, the stern and its rolled canvas just behind the rear pair). Walk him along her floor (aisle.floor_z) from where the rise leaves him to aisle.way_out.start, facing aft; empty the rear seats first. Then play one of aisle.way_out.clips at the `step` socket with its root_offset (as any place): these carry root motion (the root track: the root under his boots, from her floor onto the ground; its last key is where he stands, aisle.way_out.clips.<clip>.ends_at in her own axes): hand him to the ground battle's walking there. Play her `dismount` clip first (the board or doors open: the ways out are checked so). The Truck carries men with her tilt stowed (swap `tilt` off).

way_out.open_first: play her `dismount` clip (it opens the tailboard) before the first man reaches the start

Truck.headroom: under her tilt 1.59 m over the floor, its rear opening 1.45: she carries men with it stowed (swap tilt off); a man under it creeps (head under 1.45)

way_out.open_first: play her `dismount` clip (it opens the stern doors) before the first man reaches the start

Hanomag.headroom: open-topped; the canvas rolled across the top of her stern is 1.18 over the floor at the doors: out_doors_* duck under it from their start

way_out.open_first: play her `dismount` clip (it opens the stern door) before the first man reaches the start

M3Halftrack.headroom: open-topped; her machine gun stands over the aisle 0.94-1.15 over the floor from 0.95 behind its pedestal (x -0.95) to the cab; the canvas rolled across the top of her stern is only 0.79 over the floor at the door: out_door_* squat under it from their start
